questionText:
Consider a network using the sliding window protocol with a link bandwidth of $10\text{ Mbps}$ and a one-way propagation delay of $20\text{ ms}$. The frame size is $1000\text{ bytes}$.

The minimum sender window size (in terms of number of frames) required to achieve $100\%$ channel utilization is ________.
explanation:
To achieve $100\%$ channel utilization in a sliding window protocol, the sender window size $W$ must be sufficient to fill the link during the Round-Trip Time ($RTT$).

Given Data:
• Bandwidth ($B$) = $10\text{ Mbps} = 10^7\text{ bits/sec}$
• One-way propagation delay ($T_p$) = $20\text{ ms} = 0.02\text{ sec}$
• Frame size ($L$) = $1000\text{ bytes} = 8000\text{ bits}$

Step 1: Calculate Round-Trip Time ($RTT$)
$RTT = 2 \times T_p = 2 \times 20\text{ ms} = 40\text{ ms} = 0.04\text{ sec}$

Step 2: Calculate Bandwidth-Delay Product ($BDP$)
$BDP = B \times RTT = 10^7\text{ bits/sec} \times 0.04\text{ sec} = 400,000\text{ bits}$

Step 3: Calculate Minimum Window Size ($W$)
$W = \frac{BDP}{\text{Frame Size}} = \frac{400,000\text{ bits}}{8000\text{ bits}} = 50\text{ frames}$

Thus, the minimum window size required to achieve maximum utilization is 50.
